svg.title: Board B — Floating gate driver
svg.desc: Service schematic for the Private Reserve Board B Perma-Proto 1/2. Earth LED island and floating −70V domain. U1 6N137, Q2 PN2222A fail-off, U3 TC4426, U4 4N35, Q3 2N7000TA. T1–T11.
svg.text: Private Reserve · as-built Adafruit Perma-Proto 1/2 (cols 1–30) · earth LED island + floating −70V domain · Rev 2026-08-22
Two galvanic domains. Never join MCU_GND to −70V.
Cols 1–5 are earth (PWM, DIR, MCU_GND). Cols 6–30 float on −70V (+12V_GD, +5V_ISO). After the HDR negatives bond to −70V, both floating supplies are hazardous relative to earth. Isolated probe only.
U1 left, U4 right on the proto. Isolation barrier at column 5. No +70V, SW, or motor copper on this board.
+12V_GD U3 VDD · Q2 bias · K1 coil+
−70V U3 GND · Q2 E · Q3 S · U1 pin 5 · not MCU_GND
as-built: T1–T3 upper left · T6–T7 lower left
LED off / U1 release: Q2 on → gate off.
LED on: Q2 off, Rc2 pulls IN A HIGH.
100 nF + 1 µF at pins 6–3 · 47 µF nearby
U3 OUT B → Board C T3
block. T8 is earth; T9 is floating.
Do not jumper those two screws.
DIR LOW / open / dark U4 → Q3 off, K1 released.
as-built lower right · D5 on these screws
Do not route coil current through T9.
lives on Board A, not here.
As-built screws: UL T1 +12V · T2 12V− · T3 −70V · top T4 PWM · T5 GND · LL T6 +5V · T7 5V− · UR T8 DIR · T9 PWM out · LR T10 Coil− · T11 Coil+
Dashed outline. Not on Board B copper.
T5 PWM GPIO16 → Board B T4
T6 DIR GPIO21 → Board B T8
3-pin earth cable. No floating supply on it.
R7 10 kΩ holds DIR low if A is dark.
Feeds U3, Q2 bias, K1 coil, U4 collector.
U1 VCC and VE only. Not MCU_GND.
T3 GATE ← Board B T9 (100 Ω on B)
Q1 source / U3 pin 3 share this return.
Rgs 10 kΩ and Dz BZX85C15 sit on C.
Coil on this drawing. Contacts on Board C.
PWM off, wait for current decay, switch K1,
Housing DC13 does not rate 140 VDC / 2 A.
Q1 IRFP460 · D9 · TVS1 · SW · motor leads
ACS712 and F1 stay on the DIN HV island.
Loss of +5V_EARTH extinguishes U1 LED → Q2 on → gate off. Prove +5V_ISO-loss fail-off on the bench before 140 V. An open Rb2 or reversed Q2 can command continuous full duty.
